{
  "strategy": "Attempt 3 moves exactly one axis that has never been moved alone in this run: the column-information / preprocessing axis, on the best-scoring configuration so far. Refit hist_gbdt with iteration 1's exact hyperparameters (max_iter 400, learning_rate 0.06, max_leaf_nodes 31, l2_regularization 1.0, class_weight 'balanced', early_stopping false so all 29,304 training rows are fitted) and change only preprocessing: impute='median' instead of 'none', plus missing_count=true so the model gets one aggregate column counting how many of that row's fields (workclass, occupation, native-country are the three with missingness) were not measured — something per-column NaN splits cannot express. scale stays false (trees are scale-invariant) and missing_indicator stays false, since it is established as redundant only under impute:none but here would add 14 columns whose value is unestablished and would confound the single-lever reading. Read roc_auc, pr_auc and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut against iteration 1's 0.9272 / 0.8288 / 0.8451: any movement is attributable to the columns alone, since family and hyperparameters are byte-identical to the best attempt. cut_headroom is expected to stay near 0.001-0.002, confirming again that the shortfall to 0.9194 lives in the ranking, and this attempt bounds how much of that ranking the executor's only information lever can buy.",

  "changes_from_last": "Versus iteration 2: back from xgboost (which lost 0.0059 balanced_accuracy and 0.0046 roc_auc) to hist_gbdt, dropping n_estimators 800 / max_depth 8 / min_child_weight 5 / subsample 0.8 / colsample_bytree 0.8 / reg_lambda 2.0 / scale_pos_weight 3.18 in favour of iteration 1's settings. Versus iteration 1 (same model and same hyperparameters): preprocessing changes from impute='none' to impute='median', and missing_count goes from false to true — the only differences, so this is a clean single-lever measurement of the column-information axis, which no attempt here has measured on its own.",
  "rationale": "Both prior attempts show the operating point is already spent: cut_headroom 0.000936 (it 1) and 0.002225 (it 2) against a remaining gap of ~0.075, and recall<path> are nearly symmetric under class_weight='balanced', so pushing the imbalance lever further trades one term of balanced_accuracy for the other. The gap is therefore in the ranking. Family swap has now been priced on this dataset: the two families' balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut span only 0.8405-0.8451 (0.0046) while 0.0743 remains, so a third family is not a credible route and repeating a family swap would burn an attempt on a lever with measured size ~6% of the shortfall. Hyperparameter capacity was also tested: depth 8 / 800 rounds raised train_val_gap from 0.044 to 0.089 while validation fell, so extra capacity in this family converts to variance, not ranking. That leaves the one axis the executor still offers and that has never been isolated here — what the columns say. Median imputation makes the three missing-value columns' one-hot NaN branches explicit numeric values rather than tree NaN branches, and missing_count adds a cross-column aggregate the per-column splits cannot represent. The documented sizes for this lever are unstable (0.0097 roc_auc under a random split, +0.0011 with the interval spanning zero under a contiguous one), so no gain is claimed in advance; on adult, missingness is nonresponse rather than a recording regime, which is why the aggregate count is at least a legitimate signal rather than split leakage. Honest expectation: 0.9194 is very likely out of reach with the levers this executor exposes (family width 0.0046, cut_headroom 0.002, capacity already saturated); this attempt makes the ranking ceiling attributable and preserves the best configuration as fallback. Cost is trivial (~13 s, well inside 600 s and 2 GB).",
